text:
Yara: Noticed some weird token-level stalls when we do compact-on-demote + host-offload. Looks like compaction and host staging are fighting for the same host-pool pages and we get short stops (~40-100ms).
Ken: Interesting. We've mostly treated compaction and offload as independent. Do you have a trace that shows both happening concurrently?
Yara: Yep, snippet below. Two actors: compactor and offloader.
```
[2026-05-05T07:22:11.010Z] compactor: slab_compact(start)
[2026-05-05T07:22:11.045Z] offload: demote tenant=zephyr size=32KB
[2026-05-05T07:22:11.047Z] hostpool: acquire blocking -> 78ms
[2026-05-05T07:22:11.130Z] compactor: moved pages=12
[2026-05-05T07:22:11.140Z] runtime: resume
```
Iris: So compactor holds some locks and the offloader blocks on host allocation. The compaction increases host allocation pressure (temporarily), causing hostpool latency.
Vik: Two axes: avoid blocking hot pipeline threads on hostpool, and coordinate compaction to respect offload pressure.
Ken: Agreed. Short-term we can switch host_acquire to non-blocking for the offload path and use a placeholder token. If placeholder created, runtime treats as cache-miss and recomputes or falls back.
Yara: But compaction still can cause host memory pressure spikes. Maybe compactor should be backpressure-aware: consult host_pending_bytes before starting large compacts.
Iris: We can expose a compaction_budget API: compactor calls hostpool->reserve_compact(bytes) which fails fast if pending+reserved > threshold. That prevents compaction from pushing host into heavy IO.
Vik: Design sketch: 1) offload.acquire(mode=nonblocking) returns {ok, pending, fail} 2) placeholder lifecycle: {id, tenant, bytes, state=[pending,ready,cancelled], created_ts, ready_ts} 3) compactor uses hostpool->reserve_compact(n) and yields if reservation denied. 4) global pending cap and per-tenant cap.
Ken: Need to think about ordering: compaction may free pages that offload wants to allocate, but if compactor reserved but then fails, we should avoid deadlocks. Reserve must be optimistic and timeout-based.
Yara: Also we observed a pathological case: many small demotes in quick succession cause many tiny placeholders that GC churns. We should coalesce small demote requests per-tenant into batched host writes.
Iris: Agreed. Add coalescing window: coalesce_ms default 10ms and per-tenant batch_max_bytes default 64KB. Coalesce only for small demotes (<8KB). That reduces IOPS and host allocation ops.
Vik: Telemetry: emit compaction_reserve_rejected, placeholder_coalesced_count, host_pending_bytes, placeholder_wait_ms histogram, compactor_backoff_ms. Also route-level metric fallback_on_placeholder.
Ken: Crash semantics: on process restart orphaned placeholders need tombstones. Offloader should write a small tombstone entry to durable queue before starting copy so recovery can decide resume vs cancel. Tombstone format minimal: {lease_id, tenant, bytes, state}.
Yara: For correctness when placeholder exists and a read arrives mid-copy we want deterministic behavior. Default: treat placeholder as miss and recompute. Optionally allow a strict-mode that blocks caller until ready (for batch jobs).
Iris: Also add a safety cap: max_pending_placeholders_per_tenant and a global soft limit that triggers compactor backoff and demote-rate reduction. This helps fairness across tenants.
Vik: Compatibility with routing: when offload.acquire returns pending for a latency-sensitive route, runtime should immediately route to fallback variant; for background/throughput routes it can wait up to placeholder_wait_timeout (configurable).
Ken: Implementation plan: week 1 - nonblocking acquire + placeholder skeleton + metrics + canary config; week 2 - compaction reserve API + coalescing + tombstone; week 3 - background offloader durable queue + recovery tests. Owner: Ken for POC, Iris for compactor changes, Yara for perf dashboards.
sre-bot: canary deploy requested: tag=placeholder-coalesce-2026-05-05 target=infra-canary-7
sre-bot: deploy result: success on 4/4 canaries
Yara: Ran synthetic mixed-size chat workload with coalesce_ms=10ms and demote_cooldown=300ms: P99 down ~55%, host_pending_bytes peaked lower, but we saw one canary node with slightly elevated NVMe write latency.
Iris: Lower coalesce batch_max_bytes on that node and add a per-node NVMe health check before scheduling big compactions.
Vik: Long-term thoughts: maybe move compaction entirely to a separate fleet with isolated host-pools to avoid cross-traffic with offload. Probably expensive but worth studying. Add RFC note.
Ken: I'll open the POC PR and include unit tests for placeholder GC and compaction-reserve rejection scenarios. Keep config flags so we can toggle behaviors per-canary.
Yara: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after Ken's PR lands and once dashboards show stable pending_bytes under 60% of cap.
